subject: Lake Titicaca
hook: LAKE TITICACA IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Lake Titicaca is not actually the highest lake in the world; that title belongs to much smaller crater lakes, and even among large high-altitude lakes, it is significantly lower than others like Lake Puma Yumco in Tibet.
angle_support: Numerous smaller lakes around the world are at higher elevations, such as the 6,000 square metres (65,000 sq ft) crater lake of Ojos del Salado volcano in Chile, which at an elevation of 6,480–6,500 metres (21,260–21,330 ft) is the overall highest lake in the world
the 280 km2 (110 sq mi) Lake Puma Yumco in Tibet, which at an elevation of 5,030 m (16,500 ft) is the highest large lake in the world.
title: The Highest Lake Myth
description: While often cited as the world's highest lake, Lake Titicaca only holds the record for commercial navigation. Smaller crater lakes and other massive basins occupy much higher elevations.
narration: LAKE TITICACA IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture the highest lake on Earth. It was closer to a title for commercial navigation. Numerous smaller crater lakes sit thousands of meters above its surface. At over six thousand meters, a volcano crater lake in Chile is significantly higher. Even among large bodies of water, Tibet’s Lake Puma Yumco sits at five thousand meters, far surpassing Titicaca’s three thousand eight hundred elevation. High altitude records are rarely as simple as they appear today.
